subject.title: [Bug] Silent fail-open when Tailscale interface binding fails on gateway start

question: Should an explicit `gateway.bind: "tailnet"` request fail startup when no Tailscale IPv4 is available, or preserve the released loopback fallback with a prominent warning?
rationale: Failing closed better honors explicit configuration, but it intentionally replaces a released availability fallback and may stop gateways during transient Tailscale outages.

options.title: Fail explicit tailnet binds
options.body: Reject startup with an actionable error only when the operator explicitly selected `tailnet`, leaving automatic modes free to use documented fallbacks.

options.title: Preserve fallback with warning
options.body: Continue binding to loopback but emit a prominent startup warning that the requested tailnet interface was unavailable and remote tailnet access is disabled.

recommendation.title: Fail explicit tailnet binds
recommendation.body: Reject startup with an actionable error only when the operator explicitly selected `tailnet`, leaving automatic modes free to use documented fallbacks.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue timeline explicitly routes the startup-policy decision to this person, while implementation history is shared with recent gateway binding contributors.
